extracted.intended_audience: NSF program officers, National Science Board members, peer reviewers, and policymakers concerned with federal research funding equity
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for ensuring fairness and appropriate distribution of NSF research support across ages, institution types (colleges vs. universities), and fields; includes recommendations for peer review composition and procedural monitoring. Focused on diagnosing and remedying perceived and documented biases in NSF funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal access for younger scientists to NSF research funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board ... continues to seek means to insure that younger scientists have equal access to NSF research funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor the essential needs of performers (including young scientists) and implement appropriate programs to alleviate difficulties. Examples of programs initiated primarily for young scientists include Engineering Research Initiation Grants, fellowships (e.g., at the Institute for Advanced Study), and targeted programs such as the Human Cell Biology Program. Reference Section V (Mismatch) for further actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and analyze age-related bias in awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hensler data appear to show a bias against younger investigators; other studies show conflicting evidence but awardee population has aged faster than total population of academic doctoral scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect and analyze age-disaggregated data (success ratios by age, professional age trends) across fields and years (see Tables III.3, III.4). Use supporting studies (NRC, internal sampling) to assess whether younger investigators are disadvantaged and whether patterns vary by discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair evaluation regardless of institutional prestige
rubrics_metrics.description: If two equally good proposals are submitted to NSF in your area, one from a well-known institution and one from a lesser-known institution, respondents perceive that the well-known institution has a better chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address perceptions and real biases by increasing reviewer/advisory-panel representation from diverse institutions, encouraging proposals from lesser-known institutions, and monitoring outcomes. Do not create sheltered competitions; aim for fair opportunity within existing review structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase representation of qualified reviewers from all institution types
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has instructed Foundation program officers to seek panel and advisory group members from all types of institutions, including colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compile and use biobibliographical sketches and curated lists (e.g., AASCU list of >700 potential reviewers) to appoint suitable college and non-Ph.D.-granting institution reviewers. Track reviewer composition (currently ~2/3 from Ph.D.-granting universities, ~7% from 4-year colleges) and increase diversity to improve perceived and actual fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow for different research productivity norms (publications) across institution types
rubrics_metrics.description: It has been suggested that NSF reviewers make allowance for the lesser quantity of previous research publications by certain applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Board is reluctant to impose formal regulations, reviewers—especially ad hoc and advisory panel reviewers—should be made aware of and allowed to account for differences in publication opportunities (e.g., heavy teaching loads, reliance on undergraduate assistants) when judging an applicant's record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize institutional constraints (teaching loads, lack of grad students/facilities) in proposal evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Severe barriers at smaller institutions to faculty research include heavy faculty teaching loads and fewer graduate/postdoctoral research assistants; much college research is assisted by undergraduates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and program officers should consider these constraints when evaluating proposals. NSF attempts to relieve teaching loads where possible, and personnel/salary costs tied to research effort are recognized as appropriate direct costs to enable faculty release from teaching duties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not favor sheltered competitions for 4‑year college scientists
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board does not favor any sheltered competition for scientists in 4‑year colleges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of separate or protected competitions, integrate college applicants into standard review processes while improving reviewer representation and outreach to encourage proposals from colleges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect, analyze, and report distributional data on NSF funding (by institution type, field, age)
rubrics_metrics.description: The study should provide data on the distribution of Foundation research funds to colleges, analyze the data to determine the suitability of the distribution and give conclusions and recommendations for Foundation procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use institutional categories (Comprehensive I/II, Liberal Arts I/II, University I–IV), compute success ratios, effort ratios, recipient ratios, and compare applications vs. awards by sector and field (see Tables IV.2–IV.6 and Table IV.3 success ratios). Report findings to Congress and use analyses to guide policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve small supplemental funds to integrate college faculty into major projects
rubrics_metrics.description: For several years, NSF research programs have reserved a small block of funds (about $400,000 annually) for the purpose of supplementing existing research grants at universities in order to permit college faculty members to perform as research associates on major projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue and publicize such supplements (88 awards in FY1975) to enable college faculty participation on large-scale projects and improve access to national centers and observatories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address perceptions of fairness through reviewer diversity and outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: A majority of reviewers and applicants thought that the NSF peer review process does favor proposals from well-known institutions; reviewers are somewhat more likely than applicants to think the system gives proposals from lesser known institutions an even chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increase outreach, publicity, and recruitment of reviewers from underrepresented institution types; encourage proposals from colleges; conduct periodic surveys of reviewer and applicant perceptions (e.g., Hensler survey) and act on findings to improve legitimacy and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge field-specific drivers of award concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that requires large teams, numerous technicians and graduate research assistants, or expensive facilities and equipment is extremely difficult to conduct in 4‑year colleges; fields dominated by team research or major facilities (e.g., atmospheric science, high energy physics) naturally concentrate awards in doctoral institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and expectations should recognize disciplinary differences: support access to national facilities for college researchers, create targeted mechanisms (e.g., supplements, visiting/research-associate roles), and avoid treating all fields as equally portable across institution types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support exchanges of personnel across academic, private, and government sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the inherent uncertainties of forecasting the long-term supply and demand for research scientists, the strategy with the greatest promise is that of systematically increasing the possibilities for exchange of personnel among the academic, private, and government sectors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote fellowships, visiting appointments, and other mobility programs to broaden career opportunities for young scientists and reduce systemic imbalances in research workforce development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize salaries and personnel costs as appropriate direct costs to enable research participation
rubrics_metrics.description: As a general policy the Foundation recognizes that salaries of faculty members and other personnel associated with the research constitute appropriate direct costs in proportion to the effort devoted to the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow inclusion of personnel costs in grant budgets to permit release from teaching duties and support research effort at institutions with heavier teaching loads; this helps level the playing field for applicants from teaching-focused colleges.
